dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Odolf!

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #Hey, Paimon, and {NICKNAME}... Thanks again for your help. At least Winslow will stop harping on about moving the graves of those knights who fought the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Paimon thought it was strange!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those winds were created by the Eye of the Storm, yet you told Winslow it was the ghosts of the Knights of Favonius...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "ghost" was none other than...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: None other than you, Odolf.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Are you sure? But he just took a sip of beer. Can ghosts drink beer?

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: This "ghost," you see, is quite distinct from what you're referring to. Dear oh dear, I thought I had hidden it pretty well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait. Does that mean... There were never any ghosts to begin with, and this was all Odolf's tricks?

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Upon my word, the word "trick" has never been used with such remarkable precision.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: I adjusted the mechanism and added a lure that attracts elemental creatures. At first, I only meant to scare Winslow a little.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: If it'd just drawn in a few Anemo Slimes, they would have wandered off on their own after a few days... Then business in Snezhnaya came up, so I assumed the whole thing would blow over by the time I returned.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Instead, it attracted an Eye of the Storm.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Yeah... That made things far more complicated. I just didn't want him to move those graves. I never meant for him to end up like that.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: So... I thanked Barbatos for his divine intervention when you two arrived!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. But if we never came...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Then I would try to drive the Eye of the Storm away myself, or tell the Knights of Favonius the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: But if Winslow found out the truth... He'll probably explode. Maybe even smash the tombstones. That's just how he's been all these years...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #You really helped me a lot, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. On behalf of the Knights of Favonius who gave their lives here fighting the Abyss, I thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... something feels a little weird, but judging by the results, we did something good.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Hahaha. Yes. If there is anyone to blame, let it be me... "The only thing that can keep out all evils is an open heart and a clear conscience." ...In the end, I could not live up to that myself.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Knowing better and actually doing better are two very different things, you know? But hey, I'm reflecting on it! If the Anemo Archon is watching... please, just let me off the hook this once!
